channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: “O tarifaço vai destruir quem alimenta o Brasil”
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) warned that potential new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, combined with existing 55% Chinese tariffs on meat and EU bans on Brazilian beef, could destroy the country's food-producing sector. He emphasized that no one is discussing this risk and that the triple trade barrier constitutes a serious threat to Brazil's economy.

item.title: A nova de Nunes Marques: gourmetizar pesquisas eleitorais
item.description: The text ironically references the 'FEBEAPÁ' (Festival of Stupidity Plaguing the Country), created by Sérgio Porto under the pseudonym Stanislaw Ponte Preta in 1964, to criticize the current trend of 'gourmetizing' electoral polls — that is, transforming superficial or biased data into refined, seemingly sophisticated analyses lacking real substance. The critique highlights the manipulation or trivialization of opinion polls in the context of the 2026 Brazilian elections, turning them into media-consumption products rather than tools for genuine political understanding.

item.title: Esquerda explora foto de Flávio com “Sicário” e amplia pressão nas redes
item.description: The left used a photo of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro alongside Luiz Phillipi Machado de Moraes Mourão, nicknamed 'Sicário', to pressure the pre-candidate for president and associate him with alleged ties to businessman Daniel. The image was widely shared on social media by PT and PSOL lawmakers, who demanded explanations and sought to damage Flávio Bolsonaro's reputation.

item.title: As ‘presas’ preferenciais do PL na caçada por uma vice para Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The PL is seeking a presidential ticket for Flávio Bolsonaro and has identified its preferred vice-presidential options: first, an alliance with the PP-União federation, seen as the 'dream ticket,' though facing resistance from the parties' leaderships favoring neutrality; as a Plan B, the PL targets someone from the Republicans party, believing it can persuade its leader, Marcos Pereira, to abandon independence; as a third option, it considers Podemos led by Renata Abreu, which might join the ticket to strengthen its congressional bench.

item.title: Defesa diz que Bolsonaro não sabia que Flávio divulgaria carta
item.description: The defense of Jair Bolsonaro stated that he did not know Flávio Bolsonaro would disclose a letter requesting support for his candidacy on social media. The statement responds to a decision by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, who banned meetings between father and son for 90 days after the letter's disclosure, a measure deemed illegal by the defense and the OAB, which argues Flávio acts as Bolsonaro's lawyer.

item.title: Flávio subscreve petição ao STF que diz que Bolsonaro não sabia que carta seria divulgada por… Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, acting as a lawyer, signed a petition from Jair Bolsonaro's defense team to the STF claiming the former president did not know his letter would be disclosed by Flávio himself. The exclusive report highlights an internal contradiction in the defense strategy.

item.title: TSE avalia regras para que plataformas previnam ataques à eleição e considera criar comissão fiscalizar big techs
item.description: The TSE is evaluating a regulation to detail digital platforms' obligations to prevent threats to the integrity of the 2026 elections, including measures against disinformation and bots. It is also considering creating a commission to monitor big techs during the electoral period, requiring compliance plans from platforms with over 5 million monthly active users in Brazil.

item.title: Defesa de Bolsonaro diz que o ex-presidente não sabia que Flávio divulgaria carta
item.description: Bolsonaro's defense claimed he did not know his son Flávio would publicly share a letter he wrote, and saw no incompatibility with the restrictions imposed by Alexandre de Moraes. Lawyers stated Bolsonaro has always complied with precautionary measures and that prior letters were written and shared without issue.

item.title: Bolsonaro diz ao STF que não sabia que ‘carta aos brasileiros’ seria divulgada aos… brasileiros
item.description: Bolsonaro's defense told the STF that he did not know his 'letter to Brazilians' would be made public, claiming the reading of the text by his son, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, during a livestream occurred without his prior knowledge. Minister Alexandre de Moraes suspended Bolsonaro's visitation rights for 90 days and demanded explanations. The letter, expressing nostalgia for contact with the people and a 'hug to all,' was interpreted as a political act amid restrictions imposed on the former president.

item.title: Republicanos suspende filiação de Rodrigo Manga e abre caminho para expulsão
item.description: The Republicans party preliminarily suspended the affiliation of Sorocaba's mayor, Rodrigo Manga, over alleged party disloyalty for supporting his wife's pre-candidacy with União Brasil. Manga has five days to defend himself; if upheld, the penalty could lead to expulsion. The case adds to his ongoing legal troubles, including PF investigations into health contract irregularities and his reinstatement as mayor via ministerial and STF rulings.

item.title: Esquerda ataca Flávio por imagem com Sicário, que integrava 'A Turma' de Vorcaro
item.description: Left-wing politicians criticized Flávio Bolsonaro over an image showing him alongside Luiz Phillipi Machado de Moraes Mourão, known as 'Sicário', allegedly a member of the 'A Turma' group linked to banker Daniel Vorcaro. Flávio denied knowing the person in the photo, stating he receives numerous picture requests as a public figure and questioned the image's authenticity, suggesting possible AI manipulation. The controversy arises amid a 20-point drop in Flávio's voting intentions among non-bolsonarist right-wing voters, per Quaest poll, raising concerns among his allies about Lula's growing lead.

item.title: PDT sela apoio a Lula, e Lupi diz que Ciro deu guinada à direita: 'caminho sem volta'
item.description: The PDT announced it will be the first party to formally support President Lula’s 2026 re-election campaign. Deputy Carlos Lupi criticized former presidential candidate Ciro Gomes, claiming he has taken a 'rightward turn' and that this path is 'irreversible'. The article is a teaser for subscriber-only content.

item.title: “Foto eu faço com qualquer pessoa que pedir, só não faço com o Lula!”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) denied on Wednesday, March 15, knowing Luiz Phillipi Machado de Moraes Mourão, nicknamed 'Sicário', after a news site published a photo showing him alongside the man accused of carrying out violent actions on behalf of former banker Daniel Vorcaro. Bolsonaro reiterated that he takes photos with anyone who asks, except with President Lula, in a controversial statement that sparked social media backlash.

item.title: Flávio votou "sim" por lei que Lula pode usar contra tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) voted in favor of the Economic Reciprocity Law, approved by Congress in April 2025, which allows Brazil to impose retaliatory measures against countries imposing unfair trade barriers, such as potential new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian exports. The Lula government is considering activating this mechanism if Donald Trump confirms new tariffs, with the final decision requiring presidential approval and coordination by the Gecex of Camex. The law permits suspending concessions, restricting investments, limiting intellectual property, and raising taxes, subject to public consultations and private sector input.

item.title: Faço foto com qualquer um, diz Flávio sobre selfie com Sicário
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro denied having any relationship with Luiz Phillipi Machado de Moraes Mourão, known as 'Sicário', after a photo of the two together was published. He stated that he takes photos with dozens of people daily and cannot identify each individual. The Sicário, who died in March 2026, was linked to Daniel Vorcaro and engaged in intimidation and intelligence-gathering activities for the investigated group.

item.title: Defesa diz que Bolsonaro "jamais soube" que carta seria publicada
item.description: The defense of former President Jair Bolsonaro claims he 'never knew' that a letter of support for his son Flávio Bolsonaro would be published on social media, stating there was no prior knowledge or agreement regarding such disclosure. The statement followed STF Minister Alexandre de Moraes' order to suspend Flávio's visits to Bolsonaro for 90 days and demand explanations over a potential breach of precautionary measures, which prohibit social media use directly or through third parties. Bolsonaro has been serving a 27-year-and-3-month prison sentence under house arrest since March 2026 for leading a coup attempt.

item.title: Defesa de Bolsonaro diz ao STF que ele não sabia que Flávio iria tornar carta pública
item.description: Bolsonaro's defense told the STF that the former president did not know the letter designating Flávio Bolsonaro as his spokesperson would be made public, denying any prior agreement for social media disclosure. According to the defense, Flávio's reading of the letter was a unilateral decision by the senator, without Bolsonaro's knowledge or direction, and that the former president has consistently complied with the precautionary measures imposed by Alexandre de Moraes. The defense also denied that Bolsonaro sought to circumvent the restrictions, stating he faithfully adheres to the humanitarian house arrest regime.

item.title: Zema defende direito de Bolsonaro escrever cartas, critica Moraes e diz que vai percorrer o país para crescer nas pesquisas
item.description: Romeu Zema defended Jair Bolsonaro's right to write letters during house arrest, criticized Alexandre de Moraes for alleged political bias, and said he will travel across Brazil to improve his poll numbers, emphasizing his private-sector background and job creation in Minas Gerais.

item.title: Bolsonaro contradiz Flávio e diz a Moraes que filho leu carta em live sem sua autorização
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro told the STF he did not authorize his son, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, to read his 'letter to Brazilians' during a live stream, claiming the initiative was taken without his prior knowledge. His defense argued there was no prior arrangement for social media dissemination and that the act does not violate his house arrest restrictions. Minister Alexandre de Moraes ordered an investigation into potential premature electoral propaganda and suspended Flávio's visitation rights for 90 days.

item.title: TCU autoriza supersalários no Legislativo com ‘teto duplex’ e desafia STF
item.description: The TCU approved, by an eight-to-one vote, a 'duplex ceiling' allowing payment of benefits above the constitutional ceiling of R$ 46,300 for trusted positions in the Legislative Branch and the TCU itself, overriding technical advice and the rapporteur. The decision was led by TCU President Vital do Rego, supported by Chamber President Hugo Motta and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, and based on recent STF exceptions for benefits such as the Gaju.

item.title: Eduardo publica foto de Flávio com Elvis
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro posted a photo of his brother Flávio alongside Luiz Phillipi Machado de Moraes Mourão, known as the 'Hitman' of former banker Daniel Vorcaro, who died in preventive detention. Eduardo criticized the publication of the material, questioning its commitment to truth and making a derogatory reference to a journalist. The post originally appeared on O Antagonista.

item.title: Defesa diz que Bolsonaro 'jamais soube' que Flávio divulgaria carta em apoio a pré-candidatura
item.description: Bolsonaro's defense told the STF that he 'never knew' his son Flávio Bolsonaro would publicly disclose the letter supporting his 2026 presidential pre-candidacy. The document, read aloud by the senator and shared on social media, was deemed by Minister Alexandre de Moraes a violation of the ban on using social media directly or through third parties, leading to a 90-day suspension of Flávio's visits. The defense argues the letter was written privately and delivered during an authorized visit, without Bolsonaro's prior knowledge or consent for public disclosure.

item.title: TCU contraria área técnica e libera penduricalhos fora do teto após pressão do Congresso
item.description: The TCU approved, by eight votes to one, the release of 'penduricalhos' (extra payments) outside the constitutional spending cap for servants of the Chamber, Senate, and the TCU itself holding director or chief positions, against the recommendation of its technical area. The decision followed congressional pressure and was announced on July 15, 2026.

item.title: O trauma que leva o PL a rejeitar possibilidade de Flávio ter chapa puro-sangue
item.description: The PL resists supporting a pure-ticket with Flávio Bolsonaro due to the trauma of 2022, when the Bolsonaro-Braga Netto ticket lost partly due to weak party alliances. Despite difficulties in forming coalitions, the party fears repeating that mistake, especially given the investigations into Flávio over the Banco Master scandal and internal Bolsonaro clan conflicts, including his feud with Michelle Bolsonaro.

item.title: Ao vivo: Poder360 entrevista Nelsinho Trad
item.description: Senator Nelsinho Trad (PSD-MS), incumbent and pre-candidate for re-election and president of the Senate’s Foreign Relations Committee (CRE), will be interviewed live by Poder360 on Wednesday, July 15, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. in Brasília. He is expected to discuss the CRE’s role regarding a potential new U.S. tariff increase, the designation of criminal factions as terrorists, Brazil-China relations, and his re-election bid. The interview will be hosted by journalists Ana Mião and Juliana Alves.

item.title: Flávio nega conhecer “Sicário” de Vorcaro após site publicar foto
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) denied knowing Luiz Phillipi Machado de Moraes Mourão, nicknamed 'Sicário', after ICL Notícias published a photo showing him alongside the man accused of carrying out violent acts on behalf of former banker Daniel Vorcaro. Bolsonaro stated he has no relationship with the individual and that the photo was taken in an innocent context, without knowledge of the man's criminal activities.

item.title: DC aciona STF para alterar marco de idade mínima que beneficia filho de Lira nas eleições
item.description: The Christian Democracy party (DC) has filed a lawsuit with the STF to declare unconstitutional provisions of the Elections Law that changed the reference point for assessing the minimum age requirement for candidates to assume office, a measure that benefits the son of Deputy Arthur Lira in the 2026 elections. The party argues the change arbitrarily favors certain candidates, violating the principle of equality. The action seeks to revert the rule so that all candidates must meet the minimum age requirement on the date of inauguration, not on the election date.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro tem foto com Sicário, aliado de Vorcaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro was photographed with Luiz Philippi Mourão, known as 'Sicário', an associate of Daniel Vorcaro identified by the Federal Police as part of an intimidation network targeting opponents of Banco Master. Mourão died on March 6, 2026, after attempting suicide while in Federal Police custody. Flávio’s team stated he does not know Mourão, that the photo may be random or AI-generated, and that it’s impossible to identify every person approaching him in public.

item.title: Como um pedido de Lula fez Cid Gomes ir para a disputa contra seu irmão Ciro no Ceará
item.description: President Lula urged Cid Gomes to run for Senate re-election in 2026 against his brother Ciro Gomes (PSDB), who is seeking the Ceará governorship with right-wing support. The decision was formalized after a meeting between Lula and the Ceará PT base in Brasília, aiming to strengthen Governor Elmano de Freitas’ (PT) ticket against Ciro’s growing lead in polls. Despite avoiding direct confrontation with his brother since 2022, Cid accepted the plea as a 'party soldier,' entering a historic familial electoral battle in Ceará.

item.title: Oposição protocola novo pedido de impeachment contra Moraes
item.description: The leader of the Opposition in the Chamber, Deputy Cabo Gilberto (PL-PB), filed an impeachment request against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes for suspending Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s 90-day visit to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro. The suspension was based on Flávio’s social media post sharing a letter from Jair Bolsonaro, which Moraes ruled violated a ban on third-party use of social media by the former president. The opposition claims this constitutes an abuse of power by Moraes.

item.title: O Brasil está preparado para derrotar novamente o bolsonarismo
item.description: The article discusses Brazil's preparedness to confront bolsonarism in the 2026 elections, emphasizing the need to strengthen democratic institutions and broaden civic participation. Josué Medeiros argues that resisting authoritarianism depends on a broad progressive front focused on social justice and democratic defense. He highlights the importance of electoral monitoring and political education to prevent setbacks.

item.title: Caso de família ou disputa por poder: pesquisa mede briga Flávio x Michelle
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows that 49% of voters are aware of Michelle Bolsonaro's video criticizing Flávio Bolsonaro, while 33% know of the senator's apology video. 45% believe Michelle was right to publish the content, compared to 38% who think she was wrong. For 34%, her main motivation was the desire to run for president in 2026 in place of Flávio. Furthermore, 42% of voters tend to side with Michelle in the family dispute, while only 18% support Flávio. Lula leads presidential voting intentions for 2026 in all tested scenarios.

item.title: Lula deve deixar nova indicação de Messias ao STF para depois das eleições
item.description: President Lula intends to delay the nomination of Attorney General Jorge Messias to the STF until after the 2026 elections, due to ongoing tensions with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, whose relationship with the Planalto Palace remains strained. The move follows a government-Chamber agreement to bury a controversial Senate bill on rural debts, which Alcolumbre viewed negatively and may provoke retaliation. If re-elected, Lula could appoint up to four justices to the STF by 2030, significantly altering the Court’s ideological balance.

item.title: A estratégia de Portinho para fortalecer sua candidatura ao Senado pelo Rio
item.description: Senator Carlos Portinho was selected by the PL to run for re-election to the Senate from Rio de Janeiro after months of deadlock. He is considering two names for his ticket as alternates: Samuel Malafaia, a state deputy and brother of Silas Malafaia, and Rogéria Bolsonaro, mother of presidential pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro. The inclusion of these figures aims to appeal to conservative voters, despite Portinho being perceived as a more moderate figure within the bolsonarist movement.

item.title: Câmara aprova projeto que impede prescrição de pena para condenados foragidos em meio ao avanço da pauta da segurança pública
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved a bill that suspends the statute of limitations for the execution of sentences for convicted individuals who flee prison or have conditional release revoked, preventing the time spent as a fugitive from counting toward prescription. The proposal, authored by Deputy Kim Kataguiri, now moves to the Senate and emerges amid rising public focus on security as a central issue in the 2026 elections, with 31% of Brazilians citing violence as their top concern, according to the Genial/Quaest poll.

item.title: Câmara aprova o uso de trajes tradicionais em fotos de documentos
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved a bill allowing traditional attire, such as headdresses and turbants, in official identification document photos, provided facial recognition is not hindered. The measure, proposed by Célia Xakriabá and reported by Sônia Guajajara, aims to end discrimination against Indigenous and traditional peoples. The text now proceeds to the Senate.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Parece que todos boicotam Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign is facing deep internal isolation, with allies and family members like Michelle Bolsonaro, Damares Alves, and alleged leaks from investigators working against him. Despite this, he maintains a relatively high standing in polls, suggesting his candidacy may serve as a sacrificial pawn to position the Bolsonaro family for future strength in 2030.

item.title: Rio começa a pagar dívida bilionária com a União sob as regras do Propag
item.description: The Rio de Janeiro state government began paying the first installment of its debt to the federal government under the Propag program, reducing monthly payments from R$ 436 million to R$ 119 million. By opting to pay 20% of its total debt, the state reduced its outstanding balance from R$ 210.6 billion to R$ 168.5 billion, with adjustments based solely on IPCA and zero interest. The measure is expected to save over R$ 6 billion in 2026 and up to R$ 12 billion in 2027, helping address a projected R$ 19 billion deficit this year.

item.title: Renan Santos critica pesquisa da Quaest: "Instituto não é sério"
item.description: Renan Santos (Mission) criticized a Quaest poll showing his name recognition dropped from 30% to 23%, calling the institute unserious despite claiming he is the fastest-growing candidate on social media. He also accused Quaest of manipulating data to favor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD-GO), whose recognition rose from 52% to 56%, suggesting the increase was due to investments by Gilberto Kassab to position Caiado as a replacement for Flávio Dino.

item.title: Quaest: maioria não vê Flávio como o mais moderado do clã Bolsonaro
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll reveals that only 33% of voters view Flávio Bolsonaro as more moderate than other Bolsonaro family members, down 6 points from June. His rejection rate rose to 57%, leading among pre-candidates, while Lula holds an 8-point lead in a potential second-round runoff (45% to 37%). The rift with Michelle Bolsonaro is viewed negatively by 42% of voters, who side more with her than with him.

item.title: Tabata diz que PL da Misoginia virou ‘moeda de troca’ e cobra votação antes do recesso
item.description: Deputy Tabata Amaral stated that the Misogyny Bill, which criminalizes misogyny and was unanimously approved in the Senate, is being used as a 'bargaining chip' by lawmakers upset over investigations into parliamentary amendments. She accused the PL party and Deputy Nikolas Ferreira of blocking the vote in the Chamber despite a existing majority in favor, and reiterated that Chamber President Hugo Motta committed to scheduling the bill before the recess.

item.title: Oposição protocola impeachment por veto a visita de Flávio a Bolsonaro
item.description: The leader of the Opposition in the Chamber, Cabo Gilberto Silva (PL-PB), filed an impeachment request against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, alleging a crime of responsibility for banning visits by Flávio Bolsonaro to former President Jair Bolsonaro for 90 days. The complaint was submitted to Senate President Davi Alcolumbre.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro defende castração de estupradores após morte de bebê
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) advocated for chemical castration of rapists following the death of Helana, a 10-month-old baby in Fortaleza (CE), claiming she was sexually assaulted by her mother's 'ficante' and his cousin. He stated that, according to him, three children under 12 are sexually assaulted every minute in Brazil and asked what parents would do if someone abused their daughters. Police are investigating, and two individuals have been arrested.

item.title: A opinião de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre a pesquisa Quaest: 'vergonha'
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro criticized the Quaest poll released today, calling it shameful for showing declining vote intentions for him and rising approval of President Lula’s government. He praised Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, whom Bolsonaro nominated to the STF and who now leads the TSE, for proposing an 'accuracy seal' to reward precise polling institutes, implying such a seal would prevent polls like Quaest’s from being published. The tweet included sarcastic remarks about alleged improvements in social and economic conditions under Lula.

item.title: Republicanos suspende filiação de Rodrigo Manga, prefeito de Sorocaba
item.description: The Ethics Council of the Republicans party temporarily suspended the membership of Rodrigo Manga, mayor of Sorocaba, for alleged party disloyalty after he filmed a video at the União Brasil headquarters declaring support for his wife Sirlange Maganhato's pre-candidacy for federal deputy. The action accuses him of violating party fidelity and loyalty obligations.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: cai para 43% fatia que vê piora da economia em 2025
item.description: Negative perception of Brazil's economy dropped from 48% to 43% between March and July 2025, though it remains predominant. Despite this improvement, 68% of Brazilians report reduced purchasing power, and 66% note increased food prices. Government measures like IR exemption for those earning up to R$5,000 and the Desenrola program had limited impact: only 32% benefited from the tax exemption, while 55% view Desenrola positively.

item.title: Flávio exalta “selo de acerto” do TSE e reclama da Quaest
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) praised the proposal by TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques to create an 'electoral accuracy seal' to reward opinion polls that closest match actual election results. He also criticized the polling firm Quaest, without specifying the exact reasons. Research associations opposed the idea, arguing that demanding polls 'get it right' is unrealistic and could undermine their independence.

item.title: Pré-campanha de Lula tem disputa interna, e aliados travam embates do jurídico à comunicação
item.description: Lula's pre-campaign for the 2026 elections is facing internal disputes among allies, with conflicts arising in communications, legal affairs, and the definition of a potential fourth-term government plan. The struggle for influence within the electoral committee's core decision-making body is occurring roughly one month before the official start of the presidential race.

item.title: Lula iguala aprovação à desaprovação entre independentes, diz pesquisa Genial/Quaest
item.description: Lula tied his approval and disapproval ratings among independent voters at 45%, reversing a 26-point deficit from three months ago. Overall, his approval rose to 48% against 47% disapproval, the first net positive in 18 months. In a hypothetical runoff, he leads Flávio Bolsonaro 45% to 37%, expanding his lead from one to seven points since May.

item.title: Governo Lula e Câmara fecham acordo para renegociar dívidas rurais via MP
item.description: The Lula government and the Chamber of Deputies reached an agreement to renegotiate rural debts through a provisional measure, replacing a Senate-approved proposal deemed fiscally unsustainable. The deal establishes repayment terms of up to ten years and interest rates between 5% and 12%, varying by producer size and cause of loss (climatic or market-related), including cooperatives and participation from public and private banks.
